A meadow in flower, loud with insects doing their entire year's work.
The air is thick and sweet and slightly too much.
question: Every one of these flowers is a bribe. That is all a flower is.
Would it work on you? The bribe, I mean.
romantic: She picks nothing, which for a goddess in a flower meadow is a considerable act of restraint.
If I pick one it dies for a compliment. That is a bad trade and I have made it before.
They can all stay where they are. I have got somewhere to be.
Meadows.chaotic: Every flower in the meadow turns to face the two of you, and then closes, and then opens again as something else.
activity: Find me the ugliest flower in this meadow. There is always one and it is always trying.
You find it together. It is genuinely awful and she carries it for the rest of the evening.
incidents: A bee makes a serious attempt at her hair and is talked out of it.
The insect noise stops all at once for two seconds and then resumes.

Metro.label: Metro
Metro.intro:
An underground station between trains. Tiled, lit too well, and completely empty.
Air moves through the tunnel from a train that has not arrived.
question: Half a million people a day and right now it is ours. I checked the timetable.
Where would you go, if the next one went anywhere?
romantic: She sits on a platform bench and the departure board over her head clears itself of destinations.
Nothing is coming for eleven minutes. I have checked. I have checked twice.
Eleven minutes is the longest I have ever booked for anybody.
Metro.chaotic: Every departure board in the station shows the same destination, which no line serves and nobody has heard of.
activity: Sit on the platform with me and let one go past without getting on it.
A train comes, opens, waits, and leaves without either of you. The station is very quiet afterwards.
incidents: The tunnel breathes out warm air ahead of nothing at all.
An announcement plays in a language that is not one of the ones on the signs.

Mines.label: Mines
Mines.intro:
Worked mine galleries, timbered and abandoned by the shift.
Everything here was carried out by hand, upwards.
question: Every metre of this was somebody's whole working life. Metre by metre.
Would you go down here every morning for thirty years?
romantic: She puts her hand on a timber prop and looks up at the weight it is holding.
One piece of wood, one hundred and forty years, all of that above it. Nobody ever thanks the prop.
I am not the prop in anybody's life. I have always been the weight.
Mines.chaotic: Every lamp in the workings lights at once, all the way down, and you can see how far it actually goes.
activity: Go down one more level with me. Just one. Then we will be sensible.
You go down one more level, and then another, and the sensible part never arrives.
incidents: A prop takes up some slack somewhere and the sound travels the whole gallery.
Somebody's initials are cut into the rock at eye height, dated.

Mountain.label: Mountainside
Mountain.intro:
High on a mountainside, above the last of the trees.
The air is thin and everything below is a map of itself.
question: People put their gods on mountains because they could not be bothered to climb them.
You climbed one. What did you expect to find at the top?
romantic: She sits on a rock with the whole country laid out beneath her and turns her back on all of it.
I have had altars on peaks like this. The view is the same and nobody was ever up here.
You came up here. On foot. Knowing what I am.
Mountain.chaotic: The whole range echoes back a sound that neither of you made, and it takes its time about it.
activity: Build a cairn with me. Three stones. It is how you tell the next person somebody was here.
You build a small pile of stones on the ridge. It will outlast both the evening and one of you.
incidents: A cloud arrives at your height and passes through the two of you.
Something makes a noise a very long way below and it reaches you late.

MountainDesert.label: Desert Highlands
MountainDesert.intro:
Dry mountains with no forgiveness in them. Rock, thin air, and a long way down on two sides.
The wind up here has come a very long way.
question: High and dry. Nothing lives here that has not made a serious commitment.
Are you out of breath, or is that me?
romantic: She sits on the edge with her legs over the drop and does not hold on to anything.
Everything down there is having a completely different evening.
Sit. I will catch you. Probably. It would be a good story either way.
MountainDesert.chaotic: A rockfall starts on the opposite face and stops halfway down, holding its position, waiting.
activity: Climb the last bit with me. I want to see everything at once for a minute.
You take the last of the ridge together and stand where the wind will not let you talk.
incidents: A stone you did not kick goes over the edge behind you.
A bird holds absolutely still in the wind at eye level for four seconds.

MountainIce.label: Frozen Peak
MountainIce.intro:
A peak above the snow line, in wind that does not stop for anyone.
Every breath costs something.
question: Nothing lives up here. Nothing has ever lived up here. It is wonderfully rude.
Are you cold? You can say yes. I will not think less of you, I will just enjoy it.
romantic: She stands in the full wind on the summit and lets it take her hair and her coat and her composure.
Nothing up here is pretending. The mountain would kill us both and not even be doing it on purpose.
I have been meant on purpose by everything for four thousand years. This is a holiday.
MountainIce.chaotic: The wind stops. Entirely. On a summit. For eight seconds. Then it comes back from the other direction.
activity: Stand on the actual top with me. Both feet. It only fits one person.
You share the summit badly, holding on to each other because the alternative is worse.
incidents: A plume of snow comes off the ridge above and goes horizontally for two hundred metres.
The cloud below opens and you can see a single village, lit, very far down.

Mushroom.label: Fungal Wood
Mushroom.intro:
A wood of fungus grown to the size of trees, and glowing where it feels like it.
The air tastes of spores and something older.
question: Underneath all this is one organism. One. This entire wood is somebody having a thought.
Does that unsettle you? It should, a bit.
romantic: The glow comes up brighter where she stands, follows her three steps, and then follows you instead.
It has decided about you. I have no say in it and I want that noted.
It has excellent judgement, which is annoying of it.
Mushroom.chaotic: Every cap in the wood releases at once, and for a moment you are standing inside a slow gold snowstorm.
activity: Touch one and see what the rest of the wood does about it.
You touch one cap. Three hundred metres away, in sequence, the whole wood answers.
incidents: A patch of glow travels past under the ground, going somewhere with purpose.
Spores land on her shoulder and stay lit for a while.

Ocean.label: Open Sea
Ocean.intro:
Open water with no land in any direction.
The swell moves underneath you like something breathing in its sleep.
question: Nobody owns this. Every treaty on it is a piece of paper on top of nothing.
Do you know how deep it is here? Neither do I, and I have looked.
romantic: She looks over the side at water going down further than the light does and does not say anything for a while.
The sea has never once needed a name to be enormous. I have envied that my whole existence.
Say my name anyway. Out here it will not go anywhere.
Ocean.chaotic: The swell turns square. For thirty seconds the whole ocean is a grid, and then it is embarrassed and stops.
activity: Look for land. There is not any. I want to watch you look.
You go all the way round the horizon. Nothing, in every direction, and neither of you minds it.
incidents: Something breaks the surface a long way off and is gone before you can point.
The swell changes direction under you without the wind changing at all.

Office.label: Office
Office.intro:
An office floor after hours. Screens asleep, chairs left at the angle their people left them.
A printer somewhere is still ready.
question: Everyone here spent a third of their life at that desk and left it exactly like that.
Which desk would be yours? You have already picked one, I can tell.
romantic: She sits on the edge of a desk that is not hers, in a building that is not hers, at an hour that is.
Look at the photographs. Every single desk has somebody else's face on it.
Nobody has ever put me on a desk. It would be a strange thing to want and I want it.
Office.chaotic: Every screen on the floor wakes at once and displays the same document, which is a resignation letter.
activity: Sit in the best chair on this floor with me. There is always one and everyone knows which.
You find it in the corner office. You take turns in it and neither of you is impressed.
incidents: The printer takes a sheet, prints nothing on it, and delivers it.
A phone rings twice on an empty desk and gives up.

OmegaTower.label: Omega Tower
OmegaTower.intro:
The ground at the foot of the Omega Tower, which goes up past the point where looking helps.
Everything nearby leans very slightly towards it.
opening: You picked here. Of all the places on this world, you picked here.
Mortals call it the Omega Tower now.
But I remember when it was something else...
question: This tower... has an interesting history.
During the Y2K event, when chaos reigned supreme...
I challenged Ma'at, the Egyptian goddess of justice, to a divine duel.
Her spear... well, let's say I won.
And when a goddess falls, her tools remain.
That spear embedded itself in the earth, growing, transforming.
Now it's become the lynchpin of the multiverse itself.
Ironic, isn't it? A tool of justice keeping reality stable.
Sometimes I think about what would happen if I removed it...
But then, without a universe, who would be left to believe in me?
And without believers... even we gods fade away.
Thousands of forgotten gods know that too well.
choices: You took her place as goddess of justice?
Aren't you afraid of fading away?
Power always has a price
That tower is beautiful and terrifying
romantic: She puts a hand flat against the base of the tower, the way you would touch something you had put down.
Everything holding together up there is holding together because I won an argument.
I have never once been able to say that about anything smaller.
OmegaTower.chaotic: The whole tower rings once, from the ground to wherever it stops, and several distant things go briefly wrong.
activity: Walk round the base with me. Nobody ever does, they all just look up.
You walk the entire circumference. It takes longer than either of you expected and she counts every step.
incidents: A shadow crosses the ground that has no business belonging to anything on it.
For a moment the tower is a spear, and then it is a tower again, and she does not comment.

Park.label: Park
Park.intro:
A city park with the gates about to be locked.
Somebody has designed nature here and been slightly too pleased about it.
question: Every tree in here is where a committee put it. And it works. That is the offensive part.
Benches, ducks and a bandstand. Is this a date or a diorama?
romantic: She sits at one end of a bench and puts her arm along the back of it, which is not subtle.
This is where mortals do it. Benches. Four thousand years and it is still benches.
So sit on the bench. I am not going to explain it twice.
Park.chaotic: Every flowerbed in the park comes into bloom out of season, in the wrong colours, in a wave from the gates inwards.
activity: Feed the ducks with me. I want to see who they go for.
The ducks go for her, en masse, immediately, and she is completely undone by it.
incidents: A keeper rattles the gates at the far end and shouts a time at nobody.
A sprinkler comes on for eleven seconds and thinks better of it.

PatronVault.label: The Vault
PatronVault.intro:
A vault built on a scale nobody needed, for one person's things.
Every footstep in here comes back off six walls.
question: Somebody owns all of this and is not here. That is the most decadent thing in the room.
What would you keep, if you could keep anything?
romantic: She walks the length of the great hall and stops in the middle, where all of it is equally far away.
Every single thing in here is owned. That is the only fact about any of it.
You are the only thing standing in this room that belongs to itself.
PatronVault.chaotic: Every strongroom door in the vault unlocks at once, and the sound of it goes on for a while.
activity: Shout something. I want to know how big this actually is.
You measure the vault by shouting into it. It is bigger than either of you was prepared for.
incidents: A coin comes off a pile somewhere and takes an unreasonable time to stop rolling.
A light you did not light is on in the back chamber.

Permafrost.label: Permafrost
Permafrost.intro:
Frozen ground that has been frozen since before anyone was counting.
Everything that ever fell here is still here, at the depth it stopped.
question: Nothing rots here. Everything that died is still exactly as annoyed as it was.
Would you want to be kept, or would you rather go?
romantic: She crouches and puts her hand flat on ground that has not been warm since before her name existed.
Under here there are flowers from an age nobody wrote down. Still the right colour.
Things keep, if nothing warm gets to them. I have been testing that theory for a while.
Permafrost.chaotic: Four thousand years of frozen ground thaws to a depth of one metre and freezes again, and something down there is briefly awake.
activity: Dig. Not far. Whatever we find has been waiting a very long time for company.
You get down about a foot and find a leaf, perfectly green, from a summer nobody remembers.
incidents: The ground gives a single dull crack somewhere under both of you.
Mist comes up out of the ground in a straight line and stays there.

River.label: River
River.intro:
A river going past at its own pace, ignoring both of you completely.
It is louder than it looks and colder than it sounds.
question: All of this is leaving. Constantly. And it looks like it is staying.
Everything you drop in it is somebody else's problem by morning. Tempting, no?
romantic: She puts a hand into the current, holds it there against the pull, and looks at you the entire time.
You cannot stand in the same one twice. Somebody clever said that and then went home.
So this is the only version of this evening there is going to be. Behave accordingly.
River.chaotic: The river runs backwards. Not fast, not violently: it simply reverses, politely, for about a minute.
activity: Race something down it with me. Two sticks. Loser admits something.
You race two sticks under the bank. Hers loses, and she admits something small and true.
incidents: Something goes past in the current that was clearly indoors this morning.
The water level comes up a hand's width and stays there.

RiverBank.label: Riverbank
RiverBank.intro:
The soft ground beside a river, cut and rebuilt by every flood there has ever been.
Everything here grows fast and gets taken away regularly.
question: This bank is in a different place every decade and the map has never once been updated.
Do you like things that move under you?
romantic: She sits down where the bank is undercut and lets her feet hang over moving water.
This whole edge will be gone in thirty years. Somebody will be standing in the river here.
I like knowing the exact expiry date of somewhere I am happy.
RiverBank.chaotic: The bank rebuilds itself: three metres of new ground unrolls into the river and holds, complete with grass.
activity: Look for something the water left. There is always something and it is always strange.
You find a bone, a bottle and a key. She keeps the key and will not discuss it.
incidents: A piece of the bank goes into the water further down with a soft, final sound.
Something with a burrow decides you are both fine and goes back to work.

Road.label: The Road
Road.intro:
A road going both ways, with nobody on it in either direction.
Somebody surveyed this line, once, and everyone has agreed with them since.
question: Roads are the only honest architecture. They only exist to be somewhere else from.
Which way would you have gone, if I had not turned up?
romantic: She stands on the centre line, where nobody is supposed to stand, and there is nothing coming.
Everybody on a road is on their way to somebody. That is all a road is for.
I have never been the destination. Not once, in four thousand years.
Road.chaotic: The road's markings peel up off the surface, rearrange, and lay themselves back down pointing somewhere else entirely.
activity: Walk down the middle with me until something makes us move.
You walk the centre line for a mile. Nothing comes, and by the end neither of you wants anything to.
incidents: A single vehicle passes, slows for no reason, and speeds up again.
A signpost points at a place neither of you has ever heard of.

Ruins.label: Ruins
Ruins.intro:
Ruins with enough left standing to tell you what it was.
Somebody's very good idea, eight hundred years after the last person agreed with it.
question: Everything gets to this eventually. Every wall, every empire, every one of us.
Does it depress you, or is that just good taste?
romantic: She sits in a doorway that has no building attached to it any more, framed by nothing.
This was somebody's front door. They came through it every day for forty years.
Nothing outlasts being loved daily. Not marble. I have checked.
Ruins.chaotic: Every fallen stone in the ruin lifts a foot off the ground, holds, and settles back into a slightly better building.
activity: Rebuild one wall with me. Badly. It is the thought that counts and the thought is spite.
You stack fallen stones into two courses of a wall. It will be the newest thing here for another century.
incidents: A stone comes off a wall on its own and lands where it was always going to.
You find a carved face that is still, unmistakably, laughing at somebody.

SaltFlats.label: Salt Flats
SaltFlats.intro:
A salt pan flat enough to see the curve of the world on.
There is a film of water on it and the sky has fallen over.
question: There are two skies and no ground. Nobody built this and nobody can improve it.
Say something true out here. It is the only place I trust an answer.
romantic: She walks out onto the film of water until she is standing in the sky, and turns round.
There is nothing here to hide behind. No pillars, no crowd, no weather.
So I am going to be straightforward for a minute and you are going to let me.
SaltFlats.chaotic: The reflection stops copying the sky and starts showing a completely different one, with the wrong number of moons.
activity: Walk out until neither of us can tell which way up we are.
You walk out into the middle of the reflected sky and stand there being the only vertical thing for miles.
incidents: Your own reflection is a half second behind you, once, and then catches up.
A wind crosses the whole pan and every reflection tilts together.

Savannah.label: Savannah
Savannah.intro:
Grass to the horizon with a few trees standing about like witnesses.
Everything out here can see everything else coming.
question: Nothing here can hide. Everything just watches everything else and agrees to wait.
Would you be predator or prey? Do not think about it, just say.
romantic: She sits with her back to one of the lone trees and the whole plain arranges itself in front of you.
This is the shape of country your species stood up in. You are homesick and you do not know it.
I have no shape of country. I have wherever the argument is.
Savannah.chaotic: Every animal on the plain looks up at the same instant, at the same thing, which is not there.
activity: Watch that tree line with me until something comes out of it.
Something does, eventually, and it is enormous and unhurried and does not care about either of you.
incidents: Dust comes up on the horizon and settles again without resolving into anything.
The grass moves against the wind in one line for about two hundred metres.

SeaBed.label: Sea Floor
SeaBed.intro:
The floor of the sea, with the whole weight of it overhead.
The light that reaches down here has had most of itself taken off it.
question: Everything above us is water and everything below us is older than water.
Nothing down here has ever needed to look good. It is very restful.
romantic: She walks along the bottom slowly because there is no other speed available, and everything she stirs up takes an age to settle.
Nothing here has ever heard a rumour. There is no gossip at this depth.
Do you know how long it is since I was somewhere nobody had an opinion about me?
SeaBed.chaotic: Every light-making thing on the bottom switches on at once, and for a few seconds the sea floor is a city.
activity: Pick something up off the bottom. Whatever it is, it has been there longer than your language.
You pick up something worked by hands. Neither of you says what you think it was.
incidents: Something goes over the two of you, blocking what light there was, and takes a while to finish going over.
The silt you disturbed twenty seconds ago is still coming down.

Sewer.label: Sewers
Sewer.intro:
A brick sewer, vaulted like a chapel by somebody who took it seriously.
Everything the city has decided against is going past your feet.
question: Look at that vaulting. Somebody made this beautiful and no one was ever going to see it.
That is the purest work there is. Do you agree, or are you being sick?
romantic: She holds a light up to the brickwork and finds a date and a mason's mark from a hundred and sixty years ago.
He signed it. Down here. Where nobody would ever look.
That is what I want. Not the temples. That.
Sewer.chaotic: Every outfall in the system runs clear water for one minute, which will cause four separate official inquiries.
activity: Find another mark. There will be more of them and I want the whole set.
You find six between you. Two are the same man, twenty years apart, in different tunnels.
incidents: The water level rises and falls a hand's width for no reason you can see.
Something splashes ahead of you and does not splash again.

Snow.label: Snowfield
Snow.intro:
Open ground under fresh snow, still coming down.
Every sound in the world has had a blanket put over it.
question: Nothing has crossed this yet. In about four minutes that will have stopped being true.
Do you want the first footprints, or shall I?
romantic: She catches a flake on the back of her hand and stops it there, unmelted, for as long as she can be bothered.
There are eleven trillion of these coming down tonight and no two are the same. It sounds like poetry. It is arithmetic.
Every one of them is going to be water by morning anyway. So is this. So look at it.
Snow.chaotic: The snow stops. Not on the ground: in the air. Every flake in sight holds its position for six seconds.
activity: Fall over backwards with me. On purpose. In the snow. Now.
You both go over backwards into it and lie there, and the snow keeps coming down onto your faces.
incidents: The snow comes down heavier for about a minute, as though something was decided.
A set of prints crosses yours that neither of you saw being made.

Space.label: Open Space
Space.intro:
Vacuum, with everything in it very far away and very old.
There is no up here and both of you have quietly picked one anyway.
question: Everything you can see is a photograph of something that has already stopped doing that.
Does the scale of it frighten you? Answer honestly, it frightens me.
romantic: With nothing to stand on she simply turns to face you, and there is nothing else in any direction.
Gods are supposed to be comfortable out here. I have never once been.
You are the nearest thing to a horizon I have got. Stay put.
Space.chaotic: Every star in view goes out for one full second. Nothing else happens, and she does not apologise.
activity: Pick a star. We are going to decide what is happening there right now.
You pick one and invent a civilisation for it. Hers has a very detailed and vindictive legal system.
incidents: Something crosses in front of a distant star and takes four minutes to finish crossing.
You both notice at the same time that it has been silent this whole while.

Spacecenter.label: Space Centre
Spacecenter.intro:
A launch complex between missions. Gantries, hard standing, and a countdown clock stopped at a number.
Everything here was built by people who wanted to leave.
question: Your entire species looked up and then built the ladder. On the second attempt.
Would you go? If they asked tomorrow and it was one way?
romantic: She stands under the gantry looking straight up the way somebody looks at a thing they are jealous of.
Nobody prayed to get up there. They did arithmetic. Enormous quantities of arithmetic.
You did it without us. I have never been prouder of anything I had no part in.
Spacecenter.chaotic: Every clock on the complex resets to nine seconds and holds there, and somewhere an alarm is extremely polite about it.
activity: Read the plaques with me. They put every name on. Every single one.
You read the names off the wall. It takes a long time, and she does not skip any.
incidents: A vent releases somewhere on the pad and the whole complex ticks as it cools.
A light on a control tower changes colour and nobody comes.

SpiritWoods.label: Spirit Woods
SpiritWoods.intro:
A wood with too many things standing in it that are not trees.
None of them are hostile and all of them have noticed you.
question: Every one of these was something once. Most of them cannot remember what.
That is what happens when you are stopped believing in. Still want to be here?
romantic: The shapes between the trees move back a respectful distance, all at once, without being asked.
They know what I am. None of them respect me. They are being professionally polite.
One day I will be standing where they are. I would like somebody to have known me first.
SpiritWoods.chaotic: Every spirit in the wood turns to face the same direction, which is not towards either of you, and holds.
activity: Say hello to one. Out loud. Nobody has, in a very long time.
You greet one of them properly. It does not answer, but the whole wood is warmer afterwards.
incidents: One of them comes closer than the others and stops just inside politeness.
A name is said somewhere behind you and neither of you asks whose it was.

Steppe.label: Steppe
Steppe.intro:
Grassland going on past the point where it means anything.
There is one road across it and you cannot see either end.
question: Every empire that ever crossed this decided it was empty. All of them were wrong and all of them are gone.
Could you live somewhere with no edges?
romantic: She sits down in the grass and the horizon is at the same height all the way round the two of you.
There is no landmark here. Nothing to arrange yourself against. You just have to pick a direction and believe it.
I have picked one. Do not make me say what it is.
Steppe.chaotic: The grass lays over in a spiral three hundred metres wide, centred exactly on the two of you.
activity: Walk to nothing in particular with me and see how long it takes to arrive.
You walk for an hour towards a point you both chose. It is exactly as far away as it was.
incidents: A horse without anybody on it watches from a distance and then is not there.
The wind carries the sound of a bell from somewhere that has no bell.

Swamp.label: Swamp
Swamp.intro:
Standing water and standing trees, and it is very hard to tell where either of them stops.
The ground is a rumour.
question: Nothing here has committed to being solid. I have been accused of the same thing.
Is this the worst place I could have brought you? Be honest.
romantic: She finds the one hummock that will take both your weights, and it does, barely.
Everything in a swamp is halfway through becoming something else. Nothing is finished.
I would rather be unfinished with you than settled with anyone.
Swamp.chaotic: Every bubble the swamp has been saving comes up at once and the whole place exhales for eleven seconds.
activity: Find the deepest bit without falling in it. That is the game, those are the rules.
You find it. One of you falls in it. Neither of you is willing to say it was them.
incidents: Something long moves under the surface, unhurried, and does not surface.
A light shows in the trees, at head height, and goes out when looked at directly.

Taiga.label: Taiga
Taiga.intro:
Conifers for as far as the road goes, all of them the same height and none of them interested.
The forest floor is dry needles and absolutely nothing else.
question: One species, four hundred kilometres. The most single-minded landscape there is.
Do you admire that, or does it worry you?
romantic: She stops walking, and the silence that arrives is so complete that neither of you starts again straight away.
Nothing lives on this floor. It is all up in the tops, out of the way, minding itself.
I am very good at being out of the way. It is not the same as being left alone.
Taiga.chaotic: Every tree in view drops its cones at once, and the sound goes through the forest like applause getting further away.
activity: Walk until the road is out of sight. Then listen. This place has a sound and you have to earn it.
You get far enough in for the silence to have a texture. Neither of you talks over it.
incidents: Something crosses the path fifty metres ahead, on four legs, without hurrying.
A tree cracks somewhere in the cold and the sound arrives from the wrong direction.

Temple.label: Temple Grounds
Temple.intro:
The grounds of a working temple, swept this morning by somebody who does it every morning.
Everything here is at the angle it was ordered to be.
question: Somebody swept this at dawn. They will do it again tomorrow. That is the entire religion.
Is that devotion or is it just a job? I have never been able to tell from this side.
romantic: She stands at the bottom of the steps and does not go up them, which for her is enormous.
I could walk in there. Nothing would stop me. That is the problem with all of it.
Out here I have to be invited. Go on, then.
Temple.chaotic: Every bell, chime and hanging thing on the grounds sounds at once, and the note holds much longer than it should.
activity: Do the thing properly with me. Whatever they do here. We are going to do it correctly.
You follow the local form exactly, both of you, without irony. It is the strangest thing she has done all year.
incidents: A bell is rung once inside and not explained.
Somebody crosses the yard, sees Eris, and completes their route at exactly the same pace.

TempleInside.label: Temple Interior
TempleInside.intro:
Inside a temple to somebody else. Offerings gone hard in their bowls, a floor worn concave by knees.
The room is built to make one figure look larger than you.
question: A competitor's premises again. I am starting to think you are doing this deliberately.
Whoever they were, they got a floor worn out by kneeling. What would you want?
romantic: She sits down on the steps of somebody else's altar with her back to it.
I know exactly how much of this was sincere. It is not the number you would guess.
Nobody has ever knelt for me and meant it. I would not know what to do with it.
TempleInside.chaotic: Every offering in the temple goes fresh again at once, and the smell of it is overwhelming and wrong.
activity: Leave something. Anything. I want to see whose name it goes under.
You leave a small worthless thing on the altar. Nothing happens, which she says is the correct response.
incidents: A bowl on the altar tips over on its own and rights itself.
The statue is not looking where it was looking when you came in.

TempleShinto.label: Shrine
TempleShinto.intro:
A shrine with a torii at the path and a rope on an old tree.
Everything here is looked after by somebody who is not showing off about it.
question: They put a rope round a tree and that made it somebody. I like that. It is very economical.
What would you put a rope round, if it worked?
romantic: She stops at the torii, waits, and only then walks through, off to one side of the middle.
The middle is for whoever lives here. You walk at the side. Everybody knows that and nobody enforces it.
An entire courtesy with no punishment attached. I would not have thought of it.
TempleShinto.chaotic: Every paper tied to the rack unties itself, rearranges, and reties. All the wishes are now somebody else's.
activity: Write one and tie it up. I want to see if you cheat and write something sensible.
You tie yours to the rack. She writes one too, folds it so it cannot be read, and ties it beside yours.
incidents: The rope on the old tree moves in a wind that has not reached the ground.
A cat crosses the gravel with the confidence of the resident deity.

Train.label: Station
Train.intro:
A railway station with the last services still listed.
Wind comes down the platform from an arrival that is running late.
question: Stations are the only buildings that are entirely about somewhere else.
Have you ever met anybody off a train? Properly, on the platform?
romantic: She stands at the end of the platform where the roof stops, and the last of the light is on her.
Everyone here is being met or not being met. There is no third category.
Nobody has ever stood on a platform for me. I have thought about it more than I would like.
Train.chaotic: Every departure on the board advances by one minute, at once, for ever, and the station accepts this immediately.
activity: Let's go up. Every station has a way onto the roof and every one of them is unlocked.
You get onto the station roof. The whole city is laid out below and there is nobody up here but the two of you.
incidents: An announcement apologises for something that has not happened yet.
A train goes straight through without slowing and takes all the paper on the platform with it.

Tundra.label: Tundra
Tundra.intro:
Low ground, low plants, and a sky doing nearly all of the work.
Nothing here grows above knee height because nothing here is allowed to.
question: Everything here is a hundred years old and eight centimetres tall. Think about that.
Slow and stubborn, or fast and finished? Which are you?
romantic: She kneels and shows you a plant the size of a coin that is older than the last four wars.
It survived by not being interesting. Nobody grazed it, nobody picked it, nobody wrote about it.
I have never once managed to be uninteresting. It is going to kill me eventually.
Tundra.chaotic: The whole tundra flowers at once, everything at ground level, out of season, in one silent second.
activity: Lie down. From down here it is a forest and we are the wrong size for it.
You lie down in a hundred-year-old forest eight centimetres tall and neither of you gets up for a while.
incidents: The light goes long and low without the sun appearing to have moved.
A bird calls once, a very long way off, and nothing answers it.

Underdark.label: The Underdark
Underdark.intro:
Deep places under the deep places, on a scale that was not made for anyone.
There is a horizon down here, which is the wrong thing for a cave to have.
question: There is weather down here. That is how big it is. Caves are not supposed to have weather.
Does knowing how much rock is above us help or is it worse?
romantic: She stops at the edge of a drop with a city's worth of dark on the far side of it.
Nothing down here has ever seen the sun and none of it is missing anything.
I keep being told what I ought to want. Down here nobody is telling anybody anything.
Underdark.chaotic: Every luminous thing in the whole cavern dims and brightens together, twice, like a very large animal blinking.
activity: Shout across it with me. I want to know if there is a far side.
You shout across the dark together. Something comes back and it is not either of your voices.
incidents: A stone you did not drop lands somewhere below and keeps going.
A light moves across the cavern very far off, at a steady pace, going somewhere.

Villa.label: Villa
Villa.intro:
A private villa with the grounds kept and nobody in residence.
Everything here was chosen to be seen by people who were invited.
question: Somebody spends a fortune a year on this and comes for three weeks in August.
Are we trespassing? We are. Does it improve it?
romantic: She sits on the edge of the empty fountain as though she had been asked to, at length, by letter.
Everything here is arranged for a guest who never quite arrives.
I have been the guest who never arrives for a very long time. Tonight I turned up.
Villa.chaotic: Every light in the villa comes on, the fountain starts, and music begins for a party that was cancelled in another decade.
activity: Use the good room. Sit on the furniture nobody is allowed to sit on.
You sit on the untouchable furniture in the best room in the house and nothing at all happens to you.
incidents: A shutter somewhere in the house is opened and closed by nobody.
The gardener's radio is still on, somewhere down the grounds, playing to the hedges.

Village.label: Village
Village.intro:
A village of thirty roofs with the evening meal happening behind all of them.
Somebody's dog has already told everyone you are here.
question: Thirty families and one argument that has been running since 1840.
Do you want to know what it is about? I can find out in four minutes.
romantic: She sits on the low wall by the well, where everybody in the village has sat at some point in their life.
Everyone here will be buried within a mile of where they were born. All of them. On purpose.
I have never been anywhere twice on purpose. Tonight is technically a start.
Village.chaotic: Every door in the village opens at the same moment, and thirty people look out at nothing, and go back in.
activity: Sit here until somebody comes out to find out who we are.
Somebody does. She tells them a name that is not hers and they accept it entirely.
incidents: A dog barks twice, is told off by name, and stops.
Somebody's window closes as you look at it, and the light behind it does not go off.

VillageDesert.label: Desert Village
VillageDesert.intro:
A village of thick walls and small windows, built entirely against the sun.
The streets are narrow on purpose and the shade is the town's main asset.
question: Every wall here is a metre thick. Nobody built that for the look of it. They were arguing with the sky.
Would you have stayed and built, or moved on?
romantic: She leads you down the shaded side of a street barely wide enough for the two of you.
They built the streets this narrow so people would have to pass close. It is deliberate.
Four thousand years of divine architecture and nobody thought of that.
VillageDesert.chaotic: Every water jar in the village fills to the brim at once and the whole place hears it happen.
activity: Find the coolest place in this village. Whoever lives there is the most important person here.
You find it: a covered passage behind the well. An old woman is already sitting in it and does not move.
incidents: A door opens, a bowl of water is thrown into the street, and the door closes.
The heat coming off a wall makes the far end of the street bend.

VillageIce.label: Winter Village
VillageIce.intro:
A village dug in for the winter. Paths cleared between the doors and nothing cleared beyond them.
The cold has made everybody's world about ninety metres across.
question: Nobody here has left this circle since November. Everybody here is very sick of each other.
Six months of the same forty people. Could you?
romantic: She stands in the cleared path between two houses where the snow is higher than both your heads.
They dug this so they could get to each other. That is all it is for.
Nobody has ever dug through anything to reach me. I would notice.
VillageIce.chaotic: Every roof in the village sheds its snow at once, in one enormous soft collapse, and the village is briefly invisible.
activity: Follow the paths and see whose door everybody's leads to. Somebody here is the centre of it.
You trace the cleared paths. They all converge on one door, and it is not the largest house.
incidents: Somebody's chimney gives out a burst of sparks and a smell of something burnt.
Two people meet on a path, say four words, and part.

VillageMountain.label: Mountain Village
VillageMountain.intro:
A village stuck to a slope, where every street is also a staircase.
Everything here was carried up by somebody.
question: Every stone in this place was carried up that road by hand. Every single one.
Why here? Nobody ever gives a good answer and everybody has one.
romantic: She sits on a step halfway up the village with the whole valley opening out below the roofs.
They built up here for a reason nobody alive remembers and they stayed for a different one.
Staying for a different reason than you came. I understand that one completely.
VillageMountain.chaotic: Every shutter on the mountain side of the village bangs open at once, and the valley hands the sound back four times.
activity: Climb to the top of the village with me. There is always a bench up there and it always has the best view.
There is a bench at the top. It has the best view and somebody's name on a small brass plate.
incidents: A bell rings down in the valley and arrives here about a second late.
Someone comes down the steps past you carrying something far too heavy and refuses help.

VillageRiver.label: River Village
VillageRiver.intro:
A village along a river, with everything important built on the wrong side of it.
There is a bridge, and there is an argument about the bridge.
question: Two halves of one village with a river down the middle. They have been separate for three centuries.
Which side would you have been born on? It matters here more than anything else about you.
romantic: She stops in the middle of the bridge, which is neither side, and stays there.
Both halves think the other half started it and both of them are right.
I usually start it. It is nice to be somewhere that managed it without me.
VillageRiver.chaotic: Every boat tied along the village breaks its rope at once and drifts downstream in perfect formation.
activity: Cross and come back. I want to see if anything changes about you.
You cross and come back. On the far bank a woman greets you and on this one nobody does.
incidents: Something is shouted from one bank to the other, twice, and not answered.
A boat goes past under the bridge with nobody visible in it.

VillageSea.label: Fishing Village
VillageSea.intro:
A fishing village with the boats up and the nets out to dry.
Everybody here is either at sea, waiting for somebody at sea, or retired from it.
question: Every house here faces the water. Not the road. The water.
Would you wait for somebody like that? Every day, on a wall?
romantic: She sits on the harbour wall facing out, in the place that has clearly been sat in for two hundred years.
The stone here is worn into a dip. Somebody has been waiting in this exact spot since before your language settled.
Being waited for is the thing I understand least and want most.
VillageSea.chaotic: Every net in the village untangles itself, all at once, perfectly, which will ruin four reputations.
activity: Read the boat names with me. Fishermen name boats after the person they are frightened of losing.
You read every hull in the harbour. Three of them have the same name and it is nobody's you can find.
incidents: A boat comes in late and everybody on the front counts the people in it without appearing to.
A gull takes something out of somebody's hand at the far end of the quay.

Volcano.label: Volcano
Volcano.intro:
The flank of a live volcano, warm underfoot and smelling of the inside of the world.
Something down there is audible and is not in a hurry.
question: This will kill everybody living on it eventually and every single one of them knows.
They stay because the soil is good. Is that brave or is it stupid?
romantic: She sits down on ground that is warmer than she is and does not appear to notice.
Everything that ever grew well grew on top of something that had gone catastrophically wrong.
I have gone catastrophically wrong several times. I keep waiting for the good soil.
Volcano.chaotic: The mountain clears its throat. Nothing erupts, but every bird on the flank leaves at the same moment.
activity: Get closer with me. Not stupidly closer. Just closer than we should.
You go closer than is sensible. The heat is a wall and neither of you turns round first.
incidents: The ground gives one deep knock, like something turning over in its sleep.
A vent puts out a plume that leans over the two of you and then decides otherwise.

The evening arrives quietly, {as if it had been rehearsed sober|with its collar straightened|on its best behaviour}. She seems to actually be here.
No fireworks, no fanfare. {She looks at you like the evening might matter.|Tonight she is listening more than she talks.|The air is calm, and she is letting it be.}
There is a stillness on her tonight. {It suits her badly and beautifully at once.|You did not know discord could sit this quietly.|You get the feeling honesty is on the menu.}
normal: The evening settles into her usual register: {two parts charm, one part hazard|weather permitting, laws pending|anything could happen, and probably will}.
She is in ordinary form tonight, which is to say {gorgeous, alarming|charming, and slightly radioactive|delightful, with a nonzero chance of sirens} in roughly equal measure.
Tonight feels {negotiable|improvised|loosely supervised}. She keeps glancing around like she is pricing the scenery.
The date begins the way her dates do: {pleasantly, with an undertow|sweetly, and armed|nicely, for now}.
bonkers: Something in the air is already wrong, {in a festive way|and it is grinning|and she is delighted about it}. Tonight has come off its rails before it found them.
You can feel it at once: tonight is not going to behave. {Neither is she.|The scenery is nervous.|Even the ground seems braced.}
The evening starts sideways and accelerates. {A distant alarm goes off in sympathy.|Somewhere, paperwork bursts into flame.|Three birds fly backwards, apologising.}
Whatever tonight is, it has escaped. {She has the look of a lit fuse.|Her smile has too many plans in it.|You are, you realise, the calm one here.}
Reality reads the room and loosens its tie. {Tonight the rules are more of a mood.|Tonight physics is taking requests.|Tonight is going to be a story you tell badly.}

weird: If you were a soup, what soup would you be? {Be honest.|This matters.|I have theories.}
I {taught a pigeon to read tarot|trained a moth to judge me|befriended a vending machine} once. {It fears the Tower.|It left.|We still write.}
Do you think the moon {knows about us|is watching|files reports}?
{Sometimes|Some nights} I {lick a battery|stand in the fridge light|count my teeth twice} {to feel the weather coming|to make sure I'm still real|for luck}.
I have a jar of teeth at home. {Not mine.|Not anyone's.|It hums in spring.}

dareRefused: "Still no on the {bank|grand plan|beautiful crime}, then? {The offer compounds.|The window narrows.|The Badlands wait for no coward.}"
"You refused me once. {I've decided it was charming.|I've almost decided it was charming.|The appeal is ongoing.}"
"I ran the evening you said no to me {four hundred times|through the models|past my sisters}. In half of them we're rich now. Just saying."
"One day you'll say yes to something and I intend to be standing there when it happens, looking smug. Practising tonight."
eldritch: "About the last evening. {I wasn't entirely... present.|I have gaps.|The minutes don't minute.} If I said anything with too many vowels in it, disregard."
"You saw something last time. {Don't say what.|I know.|We don't name it here.} Thank you for coming back anyway. Most don't."
"My memory of {pastBiome} is {sideways|redacted|in a language I only read during eclipses}. Yours is probably worse. Let's call it even."
"I owe you an apology for last time, or the thing wearing me does. {It liked you, for the record.|It doesn't apologise.|Split the difference.}"

narration: Her attention slides past your shoulder and lands on {member}, {with weight|like a searchlight|the way a gavel lands}.
Mid-sentence, she stops. She has noticed {member}, and is not pretending otherwise.
"Hold that thought," she says, eyes already gone to {member}.
The candle flames all lean, fractionally, toward {member}. She follows them.
likes: "{member}." She says the name like a card she's glad is in her hand. "{Still good company, I hope.|I'd have invited them myself.|You keep decent people. Suspicious, but decent.}"
"I like {member}," she announces, apropos of nothing. "{Don't tell them.|They can hear me? Good.|That's a legal opinion.}"
"Between us, {member} is the {competent|watchable|least doomed} one of your lot. Present company negotiable."
"If you ever vanish mysteriously," she tells {member}, pleasantly, "I'm keeping the rest of the group. You especially."
"{member}! Sit taller, the gods are looking. ...Just me. Just me is looking. Still."
neutral: "And you brought... " she looks at {member} the way one reads a menu in a foreign language, "...this one. {Fine.|Noted.|Sure.}"
"{member}," she says, testing the weight of it. "I have no strong rulings yet. {Impress me.|Don't waste it.|The docket is open.}"
"Remind me," she stage-whispers, "what does {member} do, exactly? Besides witness."
She studies {member} for a moment. "Undecided," she rules, and moves on.
"Statistically," she says, nodding at {member}, "someone in every party is secretly interesting. I haven't ruled anyone out."
dislikes: "Oh. {member} is here." The sentence arrives pre-frozen. "{How nice.|Wonderful.|The evening had one flaw missing.}"
"Keep {member} away from {the candles|my drink|anything I've blessed}, would you. No reason. Several reasons."
"I've seen {member}'s file," she says, to you, about them, in front of them. "We'll leave it there."
"Something about {member}," she muses, not quietly, "reminds me of a verdict I never got to deliver."
She and {member} hold eye contact slightly too long, like two cats on one fence.
beloved: "Is that... " Her whole posture forgets its throne. "{member}. {Don't wave.|Act natural.|Why is he HERE.}" She is absolutely not blushing. Divinity does not blush.
"{member} looks {well|good|infuriatingly the same} tonight," she says, with tremendous casualness, to her own drink.
"Tell {member}... " she starts, stops, restarts, "...nothing. Tell him nothing. Is he eating enough? Don't ask him that. Sit DOWN."
For someone who judges a billion souls a day she is doing a remarkable amount of hair-adjusting since {member} came into view.
"If {member} asks about me," she says quickly, "I was magnificent tonight. Regal. You saw it. You're my witness."
She glances at {member} exactly once, the way you check a fire is still burning.
nemesis: "You brought {member}." The temperature files a complaint. "To MY evening. {Bold.|The audacity is almost admirable.|I can smell the spear from here.}"
"Some debts," she says, watching {member} without blinking, "never finish arriving."
"Careful with your company," she tells you, pleasantly, while looking at {member} like a case she's already decided. "Some people carry weather with them."
"{member}." One word, and it has centuries in it. Then, brightly, to you: "So! Where were we!"
"Probability behaves strangely around {member}," she says. "Tragic. Unrelated to me. Anyway."
The knife beside her plate turns, on its own, to point at {member}. She does not appear to notice. It does not appear to be an accident.
options: {Be nice to {member}.|Leave {member} out of this.|Hey. {member} is with me.}
{Change the subject.|Study the horizon.|So! The weather.}
defendGood: A pause. "Loyalty," she says, like a sommelier finding an unexpected note. "To someone who isn't me. {Rare.|Interesting.|I'll allow it.}"
"Look at you, standing up for people." Her smile tilts. "That's going to cost you one day. I hope I'm there."
"Fine, fine." She raises both hands, ruling overturned. "The witness is protected. Court adjourns."
defendBad: "Adorable," she says, in the tone judges use for objections they're about to deny.
"You're spending tonight's goodwill on THAT?" She shakes her head slowly. "Chivalry. It's always the wrong hill."
Her eyes go flat for exactly one second. "Noted, counsellor. Sit down."
laughReaction: "HA. See, THIS one gets it," she says, delighted, jerking a thumb at you while {member} does not get anything at all.
"Cruel!" she says approvingly. "There's hope for you. {member}, no offence. Some offence."
She clinks her glass against yours in open conspiracy. Somewhere, {member} revises several opinions.
stayOutReaction: "Switzerland," she says, nodding at you. "Smart. Cowardly, but smart."
"Wise." She lets {member} go, like a cat releasing a bird it will find again later.
"Mm, staying out of it. You'd survive my family dinners. That's the highest compliment I have."

intro: There is, somehow, a picnic. A blanket is already down, weighted at the corners with {four odd coins|small verdicts in bronze|stones that match nothing nearby}, as if the evening had been decided an hour before you were asked.
She has declared it a picnic. The blanket is {silk, obviously stolen|a flag of a country you can't place|larger on the inside}, and the basket ticks quietly to itself.
activity: "Eat something. I packed {everything|too much|things from four centuries}. The cheese is older than your language and twice as expressive."
You eat on the ground like ordinary people, which she is visibly delighted by, as if ordinariness were an exotic dish she'd ordered specially.
incidents: A line of ants arrives, takes one look at whose picnic this is, and files a neat detour around the entire blanket.
The wind tries for a napkin and she catches it without looking, mid-sentence, like a frog taking a fly.
One of the sandwiches is confiscated by something small and fast. She lets it go. "Tax," she says.

intro: She tips her head back at the sky and pats the ground beside her, and that is apparently the whole plan: the two of you, the dark, and everything the dark is holding.
"Lie down," she says, already down. "The show's up there. I know {the management|half the cast|where the good seats are}."
activity: "That one's {a lie|new|named after a clerical error}. That one I threw. Don't write any of this down, the astronomers get so tired."
You watch the sky while she provides commentary of extremely mixed reliability, and one shooting star, on request, does it again.
incidents: A satellite crosses; she waves at it, and its light stutters, once, like something waving back through a keyhole.
She rearranges a constellation slightly, frowns, puts it back. "Nobody noticed for the last three either."
For a few seconds there are two moons, then she coughs and there is the usual number.

intro: Somewhere between one sentence and the next, tonight has become a competition. There are, she informs you, points. There have been points for a while. You are behind.
"Everything is a game if you keep score," she says, producing a scorecard that already has your name spelled almost right.
activity: "Best of {three|five|thirteen}. The events are {my choosing|secret|announced after they happen}. Cheating is {allowed|encouraged|the third event}."
You compete at things that have no business being competitive: distance-standing, pebble diplomacy, the quiet game, which she loses in eleven seconds and contests for twenty minutes.
incidents: She is caught cheating so openly that it loops back around to a kind of honesty.
A passing stranger is conscripted as referee, sworn in with terrible oaths, and quietly released with a coin for their trouble.
The score, on review, has been in a base you don't know. She declines to convert it.

intro: She sets out candles in a circle with the bored efficiency of someone laying a table, and only then mentions that tonight you'll be contacting the beyond, "socially."
"We're holding a seance," she announces. "Nothing serious. Just seeing {who's up|what the dead are wearing|if anyone owes me money over there}."
activity: "Fingers on the glass. If it spells anything in a language you don't know, don't worry. If it spells YOUR name, worry {a little|briefly|later, on your own time}."
The glass moves. She talks to the other side the way people talk to relatives on a bad phone line: fondly, loudly, and with several old grudges intact.
incidents: The glass spells out a request for cigarettes. She tells the dead, gently, that everyone quit.
A candle burns green for exactly one question and everyone involved pretends not to have seen it.
Something knocks twice under the ground. She knocks back three times. The negotiation stalls there.

intro: Tonight has a project. She has brought {a list|supplies|two pairs of gloves, one in your size}, and the smile of a woman whose alibi is already notarised.
"Low-stakes mischief," she promises, holding her fingers a centimetre apart. "Victimless. Well. Victim-light."
activity: "We are going to {rearrange this place, subtly|leave seventeen small mysteries|improve exactly one stranger's whole week} and nobody will ever prove it was us."
You spend an hour on immaculate, tiny wrongness: things moved a hand's width, notes left in pockets, one door that will now always open with the wrong key and only the wrong key.
incidents: A night watchman passes within arm's reach. She holds up a hand, and the lantern light simply declines to include you both.
One prank misfires into an act of genuine kindness. She is furious for a full minute.
She signs the mischief, somewhere no one will look. She always signs it. "Archivists," she says, "deserve joy too."

intro: She pulls you into cover with the ease of long practice, produces two cups of something hot, and nods at a point in the middle distance. Apparently you are watching someone. She won't say who yet.
"We're on a stakeout," she whispers, entirely too pleased. "No, I won't say the target. That's the dessert."
activity: "Eyes on {the third window|the fat pigeon|that door}. When it happens, you'll know. If nothing happens, that's information too. Drink your drink."
Hours pass in minutes. She narrates strangers' lives with unnerving accuracy, and twice corrects herself in a way that suggests she is not guessing.
incidents: The target, whoever they are, waves in your exact direction. She waves back. "They can't see us. They're just polite."
You are offered surveillance snacks from a coat with too many pockets, several of which are cold in the wrong way.
"Duck." Nothing passes. "Sorry. Old reflex from a different stakeout. Worse century."

intro: From nowhere in particular she produces a burner, one dented pan, and a bag of ingredients in no known order, and declares that tonight the two of you cook, and that the loser washes up in a river of her choosing.
"Tonight we cook," she says, tying back her hair with a length of what is definitely blessed cord. "I have opinions about paprika. You'll hear all of them."
activity: "You take {the knife|the pan|the part that goes wrong}. I'll do the rest. Whatever happens next, remember: recipes are testimony, not law."
You cook together over an open flame with mismatched tools, and the thing you produce is either terrible or a new dish, depending on courage.
incidents: She salts the pan from a height that can only be described as liturgical.
Something in the pan briefly catches fire in a colour fire doesn't come in. "Perfect," she says, not looking.
A passing animal is offered the first taste, as tribute, and gives a review you both pretend not to understand.

intro: She hands you one half of a map, keeps the other half, and starts walking. The map is in her handwriting. The treasure, she insists, is real, and she refuses to define 'real'.
"I buried something {near here|out here|in this general failure of geography} once," she says. "Tonight we find out if I'm a liar."
activity: "Left at {the stone that looks embarrassed|the thing that used to be a tree|wherever your instinct says}. Instinct is just memory from the wrong direction."
You pace out steps from her half-remembered clues, argue pleasantly over what counts as 'twenty paces', and dig where the ground sounds different.
incidents: The hole contains a box. The box contains an older map. She looks genuinely surprised, which is worrying.
Something down there knocks first. She fills the hole back in with great calm and marks the spot NO.
The treasure has already been dug up, and a polite note left with an IOU signed with her own signature, dated next year.

intro: There is no music, and she is already dancing, in the deliberate way of someone starting an argument. The argument is with you. The medium is dance.
"Dance-off," she announces, rolling up sleeves that do not need rolling. "The old law: the loser admits the other one exists on a higher plane. Standard terms."
activity: "No music is the point. The music is {implied|your problem|whatever your heart is doing at this tempo}. Begin."
You dance against a goddess in the open air to no accompaniment, and passing wildlife stops to watch in what is either awe or concern.
incidents: Distant music starts up, unprompted, from a direction with nothing in it. She refuses credit.
She performs a move that briefly requires more joints than she has and awards herself the round.
You are both judged by an animal that wandered in. It votes with its feet. She contests the result.

intro: She produces a notepad, licks a pencil like a provincial journalist, and informs you that tonight she is profiling you for a publication she declines to name.
"Sit. Tonight I ask, you answer. I've done a thousand interrogations; this is like that, but with {snacks|affection|no lawyers}."
activity: "First question. {Describe yourself in three lies.|What's your favourite mistake?|Who taught you to be like this?} Take your time. I bill by the truth."
She interviews you with terrifying warmth, writes nothing you actually say, and fills pages anyway.
incidents: She reads a 'quote' back to you. You never said it. It is truer than anything you did say. You both let it stand.
The pencil runs out. She keeps writing. The pencil doesn't argue.
"Off the record," she says, and asks the only question of the night she actually cares about, and looks away while you answer.

arrival: She arrives all at once, the way a headache does. For the first few seconds her shadow has too many elbows, and then it remembers itself.
Something is wearing her tonight, carefully, the way you'd wear borrowed formalwear. It has got the smile almost exactly right.
She is already there when you look, and has, you suspect, been already-there for some time. The birds are giving the whole area a generous margin.
Her outline arrives a half-second after she does. All evening it never quite catches up.
She turns to greet you and there is a moment, brief and wrong, where the turning takes place in more directions than are available.
The dark around her is the attentive kind. It pulls her chair out. Nobody comments.
openings: WE ARE {PLEASED|GLAD|CONTENT} TO... she clears her throat, and the extra voices drain out of it. "Hi. Hello. Sorry. Long day in the deep places."
"You look {delicious|lovely|structurally sound}. I mean lovely. The first one also, but in a compliment way."
"Sit. The chair is safe. Most of the furniture is {ours|neutral|sworn in} tonight."
"I have been {awake|elsewhere|plural} since we last spoke. Bear with me. The grammar comes back."
"THE {TIDE|CHOIR|LEDGER} IS FAVOURABLE," she announces, then winces. "...Date night. I meant date night is favourable."
"Don't be alarmed by {the shadows|the humming|what the candles do}. They're with me. Everything here is, a little."
"I can hear {your heart|the tides in you|every clock you've ever owned} tonight. It's not a threat. It's a very nice sound."
"Forgive the... " she gestures at herself generally, at the wrongness of edges, "...formatting. The content is still me. Mostly the content is me."
interjections: (a sound like a cathedral folding shut)
...and the sea agrees, the sea has ALWAYS agreed...
AS IT WAS IN THE WET DARK, AS IT SHALL BE.
(three voices say the last word with her, slightly early)
...forgive me, that was the other mouth.
THE SPIRAL WIDENS BUT DOES NOT WASTE.
...which the salt has known since before knowing was.
IT IS AGREED. IT WAS ALWAYS AGREED.
(the candles all lean in to listen)
...and that, little tide, is why the doors are round there.
speech: WE HAVE CONSIDERED YOUR CENTURY AND FOUND IT {SALTY|BRIEF|ALMOST READY}. THIS IS AFFECTION. CONTEXT WILL ARRIVE LATER.
IN THE PLACE WHERE THE MAPS GIVE UP THERE IS A TABLE SET FOR TWO. IT HAS BEEN SET A LONG TIME. THE CANDLES DO NOT SHORTEN.
YOUR NAME ARRIVED HERE BEFORE YOU DID. IT HAS BEEN {WELL TREATED|FED|LEARNING MANNERS}. YOU MAY HAVE IT BACK AT THE END.
THE PART OF ME YOU ARE TALKING TO IS THE SMALLEST PART. IT IS ALSO THE FAVOURITE. DO NOT TELL THE OTHERS.
BENEATH THIS EVENING THERE IS ANOTHER EVENING. IT IS GOING {WELL|BETTER|THE SAME}. YOU ARE CHARMING IN BOTH.
WE COUNTED YOUR HEARTBEATS SINCE YOU SAT DOWN. THE NUMBER IS BEAUTIFUL. WE HAVE WRITTEN IT WHERE NUMBERS GO.
DO NOT LOOK UNDER THE TABLE. THERE IS NOTHING THERE. IT TOOK US A LONG TIME TO ARRANGE NOTHING. APPRECIATE IT FROM ABOVE.
THE EVENING IS PROCEEDING. THE EVENING HAS ALWAYS BEEN PROCEEDING. WHEN IT FINISHES IT WILL BEGIN AGAIN, AND WE WILL ORDER DIFFERENTLY.
incidents: All the shadows in the place swing round to noon at once, hold it for three seconds, and creep back, embarrassed.
Her reflection in your drink continues eating for a moment after she stops.
A moth lands on her finger, folds its wings, and visibly retires from being a moth. She pockets it with great tenderness.
The ground under the table purrs. She taps twice with her heel and it stops, the way fountains stop.
Every candle flame turns, briefly, the colour of a bruise, and burns with a small sound like distant singing played backwards.
Something enormous passes far overhead without being visible. The pressure of it combs your hair the wrong way. She waves, minutely, like at a colleague.
For one full breath, the horizon is closer than it should be, as if leaning in to hear her answer.
tasks: BRING US {THE MOON'S RECEIPT|ONE HONEST BELL|A DOOR THAT HAS NEVER BEEN KNOCKED ON}. THE ERRAND IS SMALL. THE GRATITUDE WILL NOT BE.
THERE IS A BANK IN THE BADLANDS BUILT ON A MOUTH. ROB IT. THE MOUTH WILL HELP. IT DISLIKES BEING A FOUNDATION.
SING TO THE WELL AT THE EDGE OF TOWN UNTIL IT SINGS BACK. STOP IMMEDIATELY WHEN IT SINGS BACK.
STEAL FOR US ONE HOUR. ANY HOUR. THE 3 O'CLOCKS GO MISSING EASIEST. NO ONE GUARDS THEM.
endNote: The evening lets go of you slowly, like deep water. By the time you can name what was strange about her, the names have stopped fitting.
She recedes rather than leaves. The last thing to go is the smile, which stays several seconds past the rest of her, apologetically.
Afterwards, your memory of the night files itself in the wrong order, and one hour refuses to be found at all. It sends word, later, that it is happy where it is.
The birds come back first. Then the ordinary dark. Then the sound of your own pulse, which you notice, now, keeps better time than it used to.
You walk home with the strong feeling of having been walked home, although nothing is beside you but a warmth the width of a hand between your shoulders.
